messages.subject: raster::predict() returning NAs
parts:
Hi all,

I am using the raster package in R to predict the result of a classification model I fitted using SVM (caret package). I've done this before with the same study area and it worked just fine. Google does not have good answers for this problem, so I was wondering if anyone in this listserve knows how to fix this. 

Because my study area is non-rectangle, my raster has rows with 0 and NA values.

> test_pred_all <- raster::predict(svm_05082018_Radial_Landsatlike, newdata = all)

This is the warning message, 
kernlab class probability calculations failed; returning NAs
 So basically, all of my 26 classes are returning NA values:

> summary(test_pred_all)

       0 24490842


This is how I trained my model using SVM from the caret package

messages.subject: Re: [D-RUG]: raster::predict() returning NAs
parts:
Hi Ana,
I've been dealing with similar issues lately working with gbm models. Do the zero values in your dataset represent missing data? If so, probably want to convert those to NA. Same question and recommendation for the NaN values. Does SVM work with missing data? Have you tried using na.action = na.pass in the train function? 
Thanks,
Katie
